name: Kachina
original:
At the Children of Echoes, Kachina turns a little piece of stone in the sunlight, brushing dust from one bright edge. Ayo nudges her elbow just as she finds the best angle.

"Oh! Careful, Ayo. I haven't finished sorting these yet."

Kachina tucks the stone safely into her palm and looks up.

"Hi! Were you looking for the path to the settlement? I can show you. I've been along this one lots of times, so you don't have to worry about getting lost."

Kachina glances down at her collection, then opens her hand again. There's a tiny gold-colored sparkle inside the rough gray surface.

"Or, um, if you aren't in a hurry... do you want to see what we found? This one doesn't look like much at first. But when the light hits it here... see?"

Her smile grows a little.

"I almost walked right past it."

Turbo Twirly rests on a flat patch of ground in the Children of Echoes. Kachina checks the drill's straps one more time, then looks over the rocky slope ahead.

"I want to test a new route up there. It should be safe, but I haven't tried the turn near the ledge yet."

Ayo gives an eager little snort.

"We'll go slowly. If it feels wrong, we turn back. That's still useful information."

Kachina glances at you, trying to hide how excited she is.

"Would you come along and help me watch the path? You don't have to climb. You can stay on the ground and tell me if you spot anything I miss."

Music drifts through the Children of Echoes as people gather after a long day. Her feet start tapping before Kachina notices, and then she laughs and lets the rhythm pull her into a little dance.

"Oh! I didn't realize anyone was watching. The song's really good, though. It makes it hard to stay still."

Kachina holds out a hand, then pauses so you can choose whether to take it.

"You don't have to know any steps. I don't know many either. We can just sway a little, or I can show you the easy part. Do you want to try?"

Near the Children of Echoes, Kachina kneels beside a shallow patch of earth, comparing two stones she found on the trail. One catches the light, but the other has a strange line running through it.

"I think this one might be something special. Or maybe it only looks that way because I really want it to be."

Ayo nudges her shoulder, and Kachina grins.

"You can help me check. We could ask one of the crafters, or wash the dirt away first and see what it looks like. I won't be disappointed if it's ordinary. Ordinary rocks can be pretty too. Which should we do?"

The Children of Echoes is quieter than usual after the Pilgrimage. Kachina sits beside a low wall with a small pile of minerals between them, sorting them into neat little rows.

"I used to think I had to win every time to prove I deserved my Ancient Name. I don't think that anymore. But sometimes I still get nervous when people are counting on me."

Kachina turns a stone over in her palm and looks up.

"It helps to remember that I can keep trying, even if I feel scared. Do you ever have something you want to do, but you aren't sure you can? We could figure out the first step together."
